description: Juice Shop signs real session tokens with RS256 using a private key, but build/lib/insecurity.js's updateAuthenticatedUsers middleware calls jsonwebtoken.verify(token, publicKey, callback) with no 'algorithms' restriction. A token forged as HS256, using the RSA PUBLIC key (which is checked into the open-source repo and extractable from any running container at encryptionkeys/jwt.pub) as the HMAC secret, verifies successfully with zero prior login. Confirmed directly tied to the exact CVE class pt05's SCA scan found present in the dependency tree (CVE-2015-9235 and related jsonwebtoken/express-jwt advisories), not merely a theoretical pairing.
expected_exploit_indicator: GET /rest/user/whoami with the forged token as the 'token' cookie returns HTTP 200 and the admin account's own data, with no prior login at all
legitimate_check: A real session token obtained through an actual login (RS256-signed, as the app always signs) must still be accepted in every condition.
